arxiv-1905-01715.title: A Parallel Corpus of Theses and Dissertations Abstracts
arxiv-1905-01715.creator: Felipe Soares, Gabrielli Harumi Yamashita, Michel Jose Anzanello
arxiv-1905-01715.description: Abstract In Brazil, the governmental body responsible for overseeing and coordinating post-graduate programs, CAPES, keeps records of all theses and dissertations presented in the country. Information regarding such documents can be accessed online in the Theses and Dissertations Catalog (TDC), which contains abstracts in Portuguese and English, and additional metadata.

arxiv-2104-01157.title: Real-time visualization of metastable charge regulation pathways in molecularly confined slit geometries
arxiv-2104-01157.creator: H.-W. Cheng, J. Dziadkowiec, V. Wieser, A. M. Imre, M. Valtiner
arxiv-2104-01157.description: Abstract Transport of ions in molecular-scale confined spaces is central to all aspects of life and technology: into a crack, it may break steel within days; through a membrane separator, it determines the efficiency of electrochemical energy conversion devices; or through lipid membranes, it steers neural communication.

arxiv-2108-13587.title: T 3 -Vis: a visual analytic framework for Training and fine-Tuning Transformers in NLP
arxiv-2108-13587.creator: Raymond Li, Wen Xiao, Lanjun Wang, Hyeju Jang, Giuseppe Carenini
arxiv-2108-13587.description: Abstract Transformers are the dominant architecture in NLP, but their training and fine-tuning is still very challenging. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of a visual analytic framework for assisting researchers in such process, by providing them with valuable insights about the model’s intrinsic properties and behaviours.

arxiv-2202-10305.title: Design of a Canted-cosine-theta orbit corrector for the High Luminosity LHC
arxiv-2202-10305.creator: K. Pepitone, G. Kirby, R. Ruber, A. Ahl, M. Canale, I. Dugic, L. Gentini
arxiv-2202-10305.description: Abstract The High Luminosity LHC requires dipole orbit correctors grouped in double aperture magnet assemblies. They provide a field of 3.1 T at 100 A in an aperture of 70 mm. The current standard design is a classical cosine-theta layout made with ribbon cable.

arxiv-2304-06749.title: A catalogue of cataclysmic variables from 20 years of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey with new classifications, periods, trends and oddities. 2020 A catalogue of cataclysmic variables from 20 years of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey with new classifications, periods, trends and oddities. – 7
arxiv-2304-06749.creator: Keith Inight, Boris T. Gänsicke, Elmé Breedt, Henry T. Israel, Stuart P. Littlefair, Christopher J. Manser, Tom R. Marsh, Tim Mulvany, Anna Francesca Pala, John R. Thorstensen
arxiv-2304-06749.description: Abstract We present a catalogue of 507 cataclysmic variables (CVs) observed in SDSS I to IV including 70 new classifications collated from multiple archival data sets. This represents the largest sample of CVs with high-quality and homogeneous optical spectroscopy. We have used this sample to derive unbiased space densities and period distributions for the major sub-types of CVs.

arxiv-2406-14390.title: Asymmetric Mixing Poisson Suspensions
arxiv-2406-14390.creator: Valery V. Ryzhikov
arxiv-2406-14390.description: Abstract There are mixing Poisson suspensions that are not isomorphic to their inverses. Keywords: Poisson suspensions, dynamical asymmetry, spectrum of infinite automorphisms. 1 Poisson Suspensions Gaussian automorphisms and Poisson suspensions are well known in ergodic theory [ 1 ] and other areas of mathematics [ 2 ] .

arxiv-2411-02498.title: Introduction to Thermal Field Theory:
arxiv-2411-02498.creator: From First Principles to Applications
arxiv-2411-02498.description: Abstract ——————————————————————————————————————————— Abstract This review article provides the basics and discusses some important applications of thermal field theory, namely the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. In a first part the fundamentals are covered: the density matrix, the corresponding averages and the treatment of fields of various spin in a medium.

arxiv-2505-14428.title: Interpretable Neural System Dynamics: Combining Deep Learning with System Dynamics Modeling to Support Critical Applications
arxiv-2505-14428.creator: Riccardo D’Elia
arxiv-2505-14428.description: Abstract The objective of this proposal is to bridge the gap between Deep Learning (DL) and System Dynamics (SD) by developing an interpretable neural system dynamics framework. While DL excels at learning complex models and making accurate predictions, it lacks interpretability and causal reliability.

arxiv-2507-00333.title: Scope Meets Screen: Lessons Learned in Designing Composite Visualizations for Marksmanship Training Across Skill Levels
arxiv-2507-00333.creator: Emin Zerman, Jonas Carlsson, Mårten Sjöström
arxiv-2507-00333.description: Abstract Marksmanship practices are required in various professions, including police, military personnel, hunters, as well as sports shooters, such as Olympic shooting, biathlon, and modern pentathlon. The current form of training and coaching is mostly based on repetition, where the coach does not see through the eyes of the shooter, and analysis is limited to stance and accuracy post-session.

pmc-10550517.title: Effect of moxibustion on knee joint stiffness characteristics in recreational athletes pre- and post-fatigue
pmc-10550517.creator: Yufeng Zhang, Zirong Bai, Zhiye Zhang, Peng Yuan, Yilin Xu, Zun Wang, David Sutton, Jun Ren, Eamonn Delahunt, Dan Wang
pmc-10550517.description: ObjectiveJoint stiffness results from the coupling of the nervous system and joint mechanics, and thus stiffness is a comprehensive representation of joint stability. It has been reported that moxibustion can alleviate general weakness and fatigue symptoms and subsequently may influence joint stiffness. This study investigated whether moxibustion could enhance knee joint stiffness in recreational athletes pre- and post-fatigue.

pmc-10668933.title: The Effects of Emotion, Spokesperson Type, and Benefit Appeals on Persuasion in Health Advertisements: Evidence from Macao
pmc-10668933.creator: Ling Jiang, Huihui Liu, Nan Jiang
pmc-10668933.description: Enhancing public awareness for epidemic prevention is crucial for safeguarding public health. This experimental study investigated the effectiveness of a combined approach involving three persuasive elements in public health advertising. Specifically, the study examined the interplay between emotional appeals (fear messages versus efficacy messages) and spokesperson type on the public’s response to health announcements.

pmc-10671056.title: SCARF Genes in COVID-19 and Kidney Disease: A Path to Comorbidity-Specific Therapies
pmc-10671056.creator: Sol Carriazo, Daria Abasheva, Deborah Duarte, Alberto Ortiz, Maria Dolores Sanchez-Niño, Takashi Oda
pmc-10671056.description: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), which has killed ~7 million persons worldwide. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is the most common risk factor for severe COVID-19 and one that most increases the risk of COVID-19-related death.

pmc-10860423.title: COVID-19 lateral flow test image classification using deep CNN and StyleGAN2
pmc-10860423.creator: Vishnu Pannipulath Venugopal, Lakshmi Babu Saheer, Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz
pmc-10860423.description: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare can enhance clinical workflows and diagnoses, particularly in large-scale operations like COVID-19 mass testing. This study presents a deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for automated COVID-19 RATD image classification.MethodsTo address the absence of a RATD image dataset, we crowdsourced 900 real-world images focusing on positive and negative cases.

pmc-12492280.title: On demand controlling of cavitation bubble collapse and jet formation through a free and rigid boundary arrangement☆
pmc-12492280.creator: Yurong Sun, Yuzhe Fan, Zhifeng Yao, Fujun Wang, Claus-Dieter Ohl
pmc-12492280.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cavitation bubbles during their collapse may form fast microscopic jet flows directed either towards a rigid boundary or away from a free surface. Here, we demonstrate experimentally that the jetting direction of a cavitation bubble near the opening of a partially liquid-filled capillary can be controlled by a non-dimensional stand-off distance, which is a function of the bubble position, capillary radius, and liquid filling.

pmc-12579749.title: Sigma Metric Evaluation of Hematological Parameters: A Retrospective Quality Assessment
pmc-12579749.creator: Parth Goswami, Garima Anandani, Vaishali Bhankhodia
pmc-12579749.description: Introduction: Clinical hematology laboratories play a pivotal role in ensuring accurate diagnosis and optimal patient care. Quality control (QC) is essential for monitoring the analytical phase and detecting errors that may arise due to instrument malfunction, environmental factors, or operator-related issues.

pmc-12588815.title: Mindfulness meditation as a tool for enhancing recovery and reducing burnout in elite tennis players
pmc-12588815.creator: Min Liao
pmc-12588815.description: IntroductionThis research determines mindfulness meditation promotes psychological recovery and lessen burnout amongst top-level tennis athletes. It also examines the modifying effect of psychological resilience on this association.MethodsThe use of a quantitative cross- sectional design was used where 120 of the top and famous tennis players participated (mean age = 24.8 years).

pmc-13160881.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Modelling Improves Microstructural Parameter Mapping in Diffusion and Exchange MRI Data
pmc-13160881.creator: Elizabeth Powell, Mark Maskery, Hedley C A Emsley, Laura M Parkes, Geoff J M Parker, Paddy J Slator
pmc-13160881.description: Microstructure modelling quantifies subvoxel tissue features by combining an MRI acquisition with a mathematical model, which is typically fitted voxel‐by‐voxel with least‐squares (LSQ) minimisation to give voxelwise maps of microstructural quantities such as diffusivity and compartmental fractions. Such approaches are susceptible to voxelwise noise, which can lead to erroneous values in parameter maps.

pmc-13465298.title: A continuity of midwifery care research mission, vision and agenda
pmc-13465298.creator: Yvonne Kuipers, Alix Aitken-Arbuckle, Holly Jenkins, Kathryn Hardie, Amy Corrigan
pmc-13465298.description: BackgroundContinuity of midwifery care is a priority within Scottish maternity services, yet limited evidence on key determinants and the absence of a shared research strategy constrain progress; therefore, this study aims to develop a systematic, evidence-based, and tailored process to inform a comprehensive Scottish continuity-of-midwifery-care research strategy, including its mission, vision, and aligned research agenda.

pmc-13654506.title: Response to the Letter “Clarifying Postpartum Renal Risk After Hemolysis, Elevated Liver Enzymes, and Low Platelet Count Syndrome”
pmc-13654506.creator: Jean-Michel Halimi, Grégory Lailler, Valentin Maisons, Bénédicte Sautenet, Laurent Faucher, Jean-Baptiste de Fréminville, Jacques Blacher, Valérie Olié
pmc-13654506.description: using real-world data, maternal characteristics associated with isolated pre-eclampsia and pre-eclampsia with hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count (HELLP syndrome and/or pre-eclampsia (PE)-HELLP).
